step 3: create a swapfile of 8 GiB
  swap: /swapfile, 8 GiB, twice the host's RAM up to 16 GiB, on at boot through /etc/fstab
  run:
    $ set -e; umask 077
    $ trap 'rm -f /swapfile.paisans-tmp' EXIT; trap 'exit 1' HUP INT TERM
    $ rm -f /swapfile.paisans-tmp
    $ fallocate -l 8589934592 /swapfile.paisans-tmp || { rm -f /swapfile.paisans-tmp; dd if=/dev/zero of=/swapfile.paisans-tmp bs=1M count=8192 status=none; }
    $ chmod 600 /swapfile.paisans-tmp; mkswap /swapfile.paisans-tmp >/dev/null
    $ if [ -e /swapfile ] || [ -L /swapfile ]; then echo '/swapfile appeared since admit read the host; nothing was moved over it' >&2; exit 1; fi
    $ mv /swapfile.paisans-tmp /swapfile
    $ if ! grep -qs '^/swapfile[[:space:]]' /etc/fstab; then
    $   if [ -s /etc/fstab ] && [ -n "$(tail -c1 /etc/fstab)" ]; then echo >> /etc/fstab; fi
    $   printf '%s\n' '/swapfile none swap sw 0 0' >> /etc/fstab
    $ fi
    $ swapon /swapfile

  Its manager is running, and restarting it would restart its Docker daemon and every container in it, so admit does not. cpuset and io limits apply after the host's next reboot.
warning: forwarding: this turns on routing between every interface on this host
  Other sites dial this one, so it relays mesh traffic between sites behind NAT, which cannot dial each other. The firewall's route rule relays the mesh, and its forward policy governs every other route.
